title: More Than 3 In 4 US Homes Cut The Landline
source: CDC/National Center for Health Statistics, National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) Wireless Substitution early-release reports, 2003-2024. Share of US adults in households with wireless phone service only rose from about 3% in 2003 to 76% by the second half of 2023 (CDC NHIS, released June 2024); adults in a home with a landline fell from near-universal in 2003 to roughly a quarter by 2023. Wireless-only households became a majority of US adults for the first time around 2016 (CDC, widely reported May 2016). Intermediate-year figures are approximate readings from the NHIS early-release series.
